To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a dicarba bond in the antimicrobial peptide brevinin- 1BYa is associated with a modest decrease in α-helical content, an increased potency against Gram-positive bacteria and a modest increase in cytotoxicity against erythrocytes and tumour cells.
the dicarba analogue of brevinin 1BYa displays potent antimicrobial activity and increased cytotoxicity.
the dicarba-brevin derivative has a lower degree of helicity than brevinin- but is more active against MRSA and multidrug-resistant A. baumannii.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel antimicrobial agents based on the replacement of the intrachain disulphide bridges in antimicrobial peptides by non-reducible dicarbamides.
the synthesis of a dicarbacystine analogue of the antimicrobial and cytotoxic frog skin peptide, brevininin-1BY, and its biological activity.
the design of new, highly potent, broad-spectrum antimicrobials with low haemolytic potential and reduced propensity to induce drug resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dicarba-brevin derivative is an effective and promising antimicrobial agent.
the dicarba analogue is a potent antimicrobial agent with reduced haemolytic toxicity and comparable α-helicity to the native and Ser-substituted peptide.
the dicarba bond has a profound effect on the biological properties of brevinin 1BYa, but the effect is not consistent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dicarba-brevin-1BY derivative displays potent activity against a broad spectrum of bacterial and fungal pathogens and that this may be due, in part, to a greater degree of helicity compared with the acyclic peptide analogue.

the replacement of the intrapeptide disulphide in the peptide by dicarba bond has a profound impact on the conformational properties of the peptide, but has only a moderate effect on antimicrobial and haemolytic activities.

replacement of the disulphide bond in brevinin- 1BYa with the non-reducible dicarbamoyl bond leads to a conformationally more flexible molecule, which displays potent antibacterial activity against MRSA and multidrug-resistant A. baumannii, but is associated with increased cytotoxicty against human erythroctes and cancer cell lines.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dicarba bond is a useful alternative to the native disulphide bond for maintaining the antimicrobial activity of the peptide, but the dicarba modification may increase haemolytic and cytotoxic activity.
replacement of the intrachain disulphide by a dicarba bond can be used to modulate the conformation and biological properties of antimicrobial peptides.

the dicarba bond can be used to stabilize the conformation of antimicrobial peptides in aqueous environments and can be used as a scaffold to develop novel antimicrobial agents with reduced haemolytic and cytotoxic properties.
